<a id="configuration"></a>

# Configuration

Configuration is optional. Without a project configuration file, built-in defaults apply; `config show` prints the effective values and `config path` prints the file location.

`config set`, `config unset` and `config validate` edit and check the file; `config get` reads one value. Every command accepts `--project` to point at a different project root.

Storage keys: `store.root` for the store (default `_CLABOK`), `docs.root` for rendered documentation (default `Docs`) and `temp.root` for transient inputs under `.temp`.

Safety keys: `undo.limit` (default 10) and `book.pointLimit` (default 3) bound the rollback history, and `concurrency.mode` (default `file`) selects the file or daemon backend.

Grammar keys: `grammar.endpoint` is the full check URL, `grammar.policy` is `block` or `warn`, `grammar.timeout` is the watchdog interval as a duration such as `5s`, and `grammar.language` is the default language for books that declare none. The endpoint defaults to the local server, the policy defaults to `block`, the timeout to five seconds and the language to `en-US`; the cap is three intervals.

The `asciiui.types` map names the project widget type for a generic kind. The configured type wins over an explicit generic label; a non-generic explicit label remains a one-node override.

`library.defaults` sets the values new books inherit, and the library registry stores them. `library sync` renders every registered book.

Configuration errors are blocking: an unknown key, a wrong type or an invalid value is refused with a stable code before any command runs.

```text
pecia config show
pecia config set grammar.policy warn
pecia config set grammar.timeout 10s
pecia config set grammar.language de-DE
pecia config validate
```

Badge detectors live under `badges.detectors.<id>` in `clabok.json`: one JSON object per detector with a `kind` and its query, plus optional presentation defaults (`label`, `color`, `link`, `logo`, `style`). `config set badges.detectors.<id> '<json>'` validates the object strictly and stores it; `config unset` removes it, and the built-in IDs `go`, `module`, `license`, `remote` and `version` are reserved. A shell strips the quotes of that JSON value, so `config set <key> --file <path|->` reads the value from a file or standard input instead, decodes it like every other input and trims one trailing line break; the two forms are mutually exclusive. A `file` detector accepts a path with `*` and `**` globs; `paths` takes an ordered candidate list where the first existing match wins, and `exclude` removes glob matches from every candidate. `command` and `http` are the only external kinds and are documented as the render exception.
